History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old female nurse with 7-day history of fever, sweats, myalgia, nausea, and fatigue after recent rural travel in Vietnam; requires in-person assessment and malaria screen.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent fever for 7 days with alternating chills, generalized myalgia, nausea (↓ oral intake), night sweats, and marked fatigue.  
• Timeline: Onset ~7 days ago; symptoms continuous without clear improvement despite OTC antipyretics.  
• Medications tried: Ibuprofen and paracetamol at recommended doses – partial, temporary temperature reduction only.  
• Associated symptoms: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, focal headaches, rash, joint swelling, or urinary symptoms (no dysuria, no frequency). Baseline screen-related tension headaches unchanged.  
• Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; extensive rural trekking/cycling, river and countryside exposure. Took daily malaria prophylaxis plus an additional tablet (exact regimen unknown).  
• Review of systems: Negative for chest, ENT, GI, GU, neuro red-flag symptoms as above.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical low-back pain related to prolonged desk work; under physiotherapy.  
• Recurrent screen/weather-related headaches/migraines (no acute change).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Over-the-counter ibuprofen and paracetamol (self-administered).

Allergies:
• Pollen (hay fever).  
• No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Registered nurse; struggling at work due to fatigue.  
• Smoking: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Moderate intake (exact units not stated).  
• Exercise: Moderate exercise several times per week.  
• Vaccinations: Up-to-date, including Hepatitis B.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
• No other familial illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
Not performed during teleconsultation (patient remote).

Investigations:
• Planned: Thick and thin blood films for malaria.  
• Planned: Routine and inflammatory blood panels (CBC, ESR/CRP, LFTs, U&E, others per local “pyrexia of unknown origin” protocol).  
• Further investigations dependent on in-person examination findings.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Fever of unknown origin ± night sweats after recent travel.  
  • Differential includes malaria, other travel-related infections, and common bacterial/viral causes.  
  • Plan: Urgent in-person examination at central London clinic (or local A&E if more convenient).  
  • Arrange same-day bloods: malaria screen (thick/thin films), full infection panel, inflammatory markers.  
  • Hold off on work duties until diagnosis established and clinically safe to return.

Issue 2: Possible malaria or other exotic infection.  
  • Plan: Emphasize need for prompt malaria testing; ensure labs mark sample as urgent.  
  • Consider repeat malaria films if initial negative and clinical suspicion remains.

Issue 3: Symptomatic management.  
  • Continue antipyretics (paracetamol/ibuprofen) within recommended doses as needed for fever and myalgia.  
  • Encourage adequate hydration despite nausea; small frequent sips.  
  • Advise to seek immediate care if confusion, worsening headache, jaundice, bleeding, or hemodynamic instability develops.

General plan items:  
• Administrative: Doctor to message admin team to book clinic appointment; patient to phone provided number for scheduling.  
• Documentation: Clinician to include test requests and assessment in notes for receiving provider.  
• Follow-up: Reassessment after examination and results; further management contingent on findings.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs, physical examination details, full medication list (dose/frequency), detailed allergy profile beyond pollen.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
